P0_overlay.decision: top-layer substrate (popover / dialog.showModal / inert) + deferred close as the single exit path; native CSS `overlay` and hybrid both rejected

popoverModeContract.manual: TEKAD owns dismissal -> deferred visual exit lifecycle GUARANTEED
popoverModeContract.auto: browser owns light-dismiss -> TEKAD reconciles already-closed state -> deferred exit animation NOT promised

P0_overlay.contract: 12 normative requirements in p0-report.md section H5
P0_overlay.latentHazardFixed: _hardReset set terminal state after the DOM close call; a synchronous toggle could have re-entered cleanup. Fixed + guard. NOTE: both engines delivered toggle asynchronously, so the recursive path was never triggered - the guard is defence-in-depth, not an observed fix.
P0_overlay.accessibility: close intent / visual exit / actual close all OBSERVED; assistive-technology behaviour UNVERIFIED - no screen reader tested at any point. Generic aria-hidden rule removed as semantically wrong.

reentrancy.rootCause: _hardReset assigned the terminal state AFTER the browser close operation, so _onToggle's `state !== closed` guard was ineffective during that window; a synchronously delivered toggle could re-enter cleanup
reentrancy.fix: terminal state established before the close operation, plus a _resetting guard; close operation extracted to an injectable closeOp platform seam
reentrancy.proof: reentrancy.test.mjs - 16/16 assertions, evidence class DEFENSIVE / SIMULATED (synchronous delivery simulated at the closeOp seam; NOT browser evidence)
reentrancy.control: pre-fix ordering reproduced against a local replica and confirmed to re-enter, so the assertions are non-vacuous
reentrancy.browserObservation: neither Chromium nor WebKitGTK delivers toggle synchronously; synchronous delivery by a real engine remains UNVERIFIED

secondOrderReview.scope: _onToggle, _hardReset, _finish, _clearPending, open, close reviewed as one state machine
secondOrderReview.defect: destroy() left the `closing` class on the element and state at 'closing', leaking visual exit state onto a DOM node that outlives the controller
secondOrderReview.fix: destroy() removes the class and sets state to 'closed'; it deliberately does NOT close the element - unmounting is the caller's concern
secondOrderReview.redesign: none - no other concrete defect found

P0_overlay.singleSourceOfTruth: deferred-overlay.mjs - imported by both harness4.html (browser) and reentrancy.test.mjs (state machine), so they cannot drift

fail: ngTemplateOutlet declared outside the grid (GRID missing)
content projection across a component boundary (GRID_ROW missing)
ViewContainerRef.createEmbeddedView with an outside template (GRID missing)
consumer-supplied template without an injector (GRID_ROW missing)
P1_ariaGrid.control: cdk-table reproduced angular/components#32603 (GRID_ROW missing, 4 of 12 cells) - confirms the test is non-vacuous and validates TEKAD owning L3
P1_ariaGrid.rootCause: Angular resolves directive DI by the template's DECLARATION site, not its DOM insertion point; embedded views inherit the declaration-site injector unless one is supplied
P1_ariaGrid.newRequirement: consumer-supplied cell/column templates MUST be rendered with the row's insertion-site injector (ngTemplateOutletInjector / createEmbeddedView({injector})); without it cells silently fail to register - no build error, no visible cells. Cell API must be template-based, NOT content-projection-based.
P1_ariaGrid.methodologyDefect: an NG0201 during change detection contaminated the next scenario; runner now reloads the page per scenario
